previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a large right gluteal hematoma causing pain and swelling, along with acute blood loss anemia and hypertensive urgency. She had a history of ESRD with a kidney transplant and was previously on anticoagulants. Imaging confirmed a 11.4 cm hematoma without signs of abscess. She received two units of packed red blood cells but declined further transfusions as a Jehovah’s Witness. Her hemoglobin remained suboptimal, and hemolysis was noted, likely due to the hematoma. Hypertension was managed with hydralazine and a switch to carvedilol and Norvasc. She reported a history of melena, but recent stool was brown and witnessed by staff. The patient became lethargic, possibly due to narcotics, and her mental status improved with dose reduction. She left against medical advice on the second hospital day due to a home emergency, despite recommendations to stay for further monitoring.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Other musculoskeletal symptoms referable to limbs

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with history of stroke, 
epilepsy, hypertension, and Crohn's disease with a recent left 
total knee replacement (___) complicated by left knee  
cellulitis, and s/p DCD kidney transplant ___ ___ (___)  
presenting with ~ 1 wk of increasing knee swelling, redness, and 
pain, c/w prosthetic join infection. 

ACUTE ISSUES: 
# Severe sepsis ___ bacteremia and septic arthritis/prosthetic 
joint infection: Patient had left TKR on ___, presented with 
1 week of increasing L knee swelling, redness, pain with 
development of fever to ___ and L knee drainage on ___. 
Prior to this, the patient was admitted ___ with left knee 
cellulitis for which she was treated with vancomycin followed by 
clindamycin to complete a 10-day course of antibiotics. On 
presentation to the ED here, she was afebrile, tachycardic. 
Lower-extremity ultrasound was negative for DVT but showed a 
large fluid collection 14.6 x 9.0 cm. Her knee was tapped by 
ortho for ~120mL of ""opaque yellow, foul-smelling fluid""; 
initial analysis of the aspirate showed >100k WBCs, left shifted 
with 88% PMNs, and gram stain ultimately with gram-positive 
cocci ___ clusters. The patient was admitted to ortho, started on 
vancomycin.  However, prior to going to the OR, she was 
transferred to medicine at which time her abx were broadened to 
vanc/aztreonam given + blood cultures growing GPCs and GNRs.  
Patient was then taken to OR for hardware removal on ___.  
Overnight, she became hypotensive and oliguric with worsening 
mental status.  She had an acute drop ___ her HCT, prompting 
transfusion.  She was then transferred to MICU briefly.  There, 
here abx were initially broadened but then ultimately narrowed 
to cefazolin given identification of MSSA and pan-sensitive E. 
coli ___ her blood as well as joint infection.  However, on ___ 
she was started on daptomycin once her left tibial culture grew 
pediococcus.  She did comlete 3 more days of ceftriaxone to 
complete a 10 day course for her GNR bacteremia.  The dapto will 
need to be continued till ___ per ID.  Her last positive BCx 
was on ___.  TTE and MRI of spine were performed to r/o 
endocarditis and seeding of her spinal hardware.  These were 
negative.  Additionally, her right hip hematoma from a prior 
admission was aspirated to r/o superinfection.  There was no 
growth from these cultures while on abx.  Prior to transfer to 
___, pt underwent 2 further washouts of her knee, and drains 
were pulled on ___.  Per ortho, subcu heparin should be 
continued for 1 month and aspirin can be restarted on discharge. 
 Pt will f/u with ortho for further discussion about placement 
of new hardware. 

# Acute on Chronic Kidney Injury: Patient with ESRD since ___ 
on HD x ___ years now s/p cadaveric renal transplant ___ at 
___. Baseline Cr 2.8, but increased to 3.0-4.0 during 
hospitalization ___ the setting of presumed ischemic ATN during 
perioperative hypotension as well as supratherapeutic tacrolimus 
levels. Per report, her graft had been failing as there was 
evidence of acute tubular injury or obstructive uropathy, 
without active rejection on biopsy.  The patient's tacrolimus 
was titrated down to 2mg PO BID and trough was 5.7 on day of 
discharge.  This dose was stable for several days prior to 
discharge.  She was continued on prednisone for 
immunosuppresion.  UOP was intially poor but has increased 
dramatically over the days leading up to discharge.  Her Cre had 
downtrended to 2.7 on the day of d/c, which is close to her 
baseline.

# Acute Anemia of Blood Loss with underlying Chronic Kidney 
Disease: Patient with acute anemia s/p left knee joint wash-out 
procedures superimposed on chronic anemia ___ CKD, Fe deficiency 
and ?hemolysis.  Continued to have bloody output (100-400 cc) 
from left knee drain (HCT of drain fluid = ___ leading up to 
discharg suggesting that this blood loss was likely responsible 
for acute anemia.  Stool guiac was negative and hemolysis w/u 
was negative. Notably, on ___ (morning after third knee 
wash-out procedure), HCT dropped to 12.  However, she was 
hemodynamically stable during this entire event.  IJ placed on 
the floor, as patient had lost IV access) and she received 3u 
pRBCs + 1u FFP; HCT corrected to 21.  The patient was transfused 
pRBCs for HCT < 21 on 3 occasions between ___ and ___. She 
received IV PPI prophylaxis which was transitioned to PO on 
discharge.  Transfused 1U PRBCs for HCT of 20.8 on ___. 

# Coagulopathy: elevated ___ since admission; worse on ___ 
___ the setting of HCT=12 and transfusion of 3u pRBCs. Patient 
received 1u FFP and vitamin K and was started on DDAVP for 
uremic platelets.  ___ and PTT normalized with these 
intervenetions. 

# C Diff colitis: C diff toxin positive on ___ ___ the 
setting of watery diarrhea and immunocompromised pt s/p 
transplant.  Patient to complete 14-day course of oral 
vancomycin; diarrhea had markedly improved at time of discharge.

# Tender left arm nodule with surrounding bruising: a ___ 
ultrasound showed likely hematoma with diffusion of blood into 
subcutaneous tissues, causing bruising.  No interventions 
required.  

# Gluteal Mass: Right gluteal hematoma vs. abscess; hematoma

HISTORY:  Large right gluteal collection.  On ultrasound appears complex, with
appearances of hematoma, but unable to exclude superinfection.  Please
aspirate to evaluate whether this represents an infected hematoma.

TECHNIQUE:  Ultrasound guided aspiration of right gluteal hematoma.

COMPARISON:  Targeted ultrasound dated ___.  

PROCEDURE:

This procedure was reviewed in detail with the patient's health care proxy,
with the relevant risks and potential benefits explained, and telephone
consent was obtained.  Prior to the procedure, preprocedure timeout was
performed according to ___ procedure, utilizing 3 independent identifiers
and to verify the procedure to be performed.

The right gluteal region was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. 
No local anesthetic or sedation was administered.  A 16-gauge needle was
advanced under ultrasound guidance into the right gluteal collection. 
Initially, suction applied to this needle did not yield any contents. 
Subsequently, the needle was flushed with 10 cc of sterile, nonbacteriostatic
saline and there was then free aspiration of approximately 20 cc of dark
sanguinous material from the collection, consistent with old blood products. 
After the needle was withdrawn, more old blood products continue to flow out
of the needle side.  Therefore, the needle was reinserted at the same site,
and attempts made to aspirate more fluid.  Despite attempts at suction, no
additional fluid could be actively aspirated out.  However, as there was
continued oozing from the site after removing the needle, pressure was applied
at various sides of the large collection in order to try to express more of
this fluid out.  Finally, after no fluid was spontaneously oozing out,
pressure was applied to the needle puncture site, and a sterile dressing
applied.

The 20 cc of aspirated material was sent to microbiology for analysis.

FINDINGS:

Prior to the procedure, pre procedure imaging was performed in order to
localize the gluteal collection.  This clearly demonstrated a multi-septated
hypoechoic structure deep to a large lump which was visible in the right
gluteal region.

IMPRESSION:

Successful, non complicated aspiration of the right gluteal hematoma, with 20
cc sample sent for microbiology.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with infected left TKA and difficult venous
access.  Request for a tunneled central venous line for antibiotics.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ (interventional radiology fellow) and Dr. ___
___ (radiology resident) performed the procedure. Dr. ___
(interventional radiology attending) was present and supervised the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
fentanyl (125 mcg) and Versed (2.5 mg) throughout total intraservice time of
50 minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored. Local anesthesia was provided by 1% lidocaine to the dermis and 1%
lidocaine with epinephrine into the subcutaneous tissues.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 3 minutes, 11 mGy. No contrast was administered.

PROCEDURE: 

1. Tunneled ___ single lumen ___ central venous line via a right
internal jugular approach.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient's
healthcare proxy, her daughter, over the phone and was witnessed by an
additional physician.  This was performed after explaining the risks,
benefits, alternatives and indications of the procedure.

The patient was transported to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  The left neck was prepped and draped in usual sterile fashion.
A preprocedure huddle and timeout was performed per ___ protocol.

After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues a micropuncture needle
was inserted into the left internal jugular vein under ultrasound guidance. 
Hard copy ultrasound images were saved for reference.  A 0.018 nitinol wire
was advanced into the superior vena cava.  After additional anesthesia, a
small ___ was made in the skin.  Micropuncture needle was exchanged with
micropuncture sheath.  The inner cannula and nitinol wire were removed.  A
0.035 J-wire was advanced into the right atrium.  Appropriate measurements
were made for skin incision several fingerbreadths below the venotomy site. 
The wire was then advanced into the IVC.

Attention was now turned to creation of subcutaneous tunnel.  After additional
local anesthesia, a skin incision was made.  A 10 ___ tunneled catheter was
passed from the incision to the venotomy site with aid of a plastic tunneling
device.  The venotomy tract was dilated with 7 and 9 ___ dilators. 
Peel-away sheath was passed over the wire.  The wire and inner cannula were
removed and the catheter was passed through the peel-away sheath. The
peel-away sheath was removed while the catheter was pushed into the right
atrium.  This was confirmed with fluoroscopy demonstrating the catheter tip in
the right atrium.  Blood was aspirated and flushed through the single lumen.
The catheter was secured with ___ silk sutures and ___ Flexitrack devices. 
Venotomy site was closed with 4 Vicryl subcuticular stitch.  Dry sterile
dressings were applied.  No immediate post-procedure complications were noted.
The patient tolerated the procedure well.

IMPRESSION:  
Successful placement of a single lumen tunneled central venous catheter
through the right internal jugular vein approach.  
The tip is located in the right atrium and the catheter is ready for use.
